title: Reviewing a Proposal You Disagree With
meta: B2 · 约 280 词 · 场景：方案评审

sections.heading: 1. Make Their Case First
paragraphs: You open the proposal, read the first page, and already know you don't like it.
That reaction might be real ==insight==, or it might just be ==bias== toward your own approach.
Before you write a single comment, try to __argue for__ the proposal.
**If you cannot explain why a smart person would choose this, you are not ready to reject it.**
Write a short summary of the author's goal and their strongest argument.
Then share it: "Here is my understanding; did I get it right?"
This step does two things.
It catches ==misunderstandings== early, because many disagreements are really about different readings of the same page.
It also shows the author you __took their work seriously__, which makes them more ==receptive== to what comes next.
sections.heading_zh: 1. 先替对方把道理讲出来
paragraphs_zh: 你打开这份提案，读完第一页，就已经知道自己不喜欢它了。
这种反应可能是真知灼见，也可能只是你偏爱自己那套做法。
在写下任何一条评论之前，先试着替这份提案说话。
如果你讲不出一个聪明人为什么会这么选，你就还没资格否掉它。
简短写下作者的目标，以及他们最有力的论据。
然后发出去：「这是我的理解，我理解得对吗？」
这一步有两个作用。
它能尽早发现误解，因为很多分歧其实只是对同一页内容的理解不同。
它也让作者看到你认真对待了他们的工作，这样他们对你后面的意见会更听得进去。

sections.heading: 2. Different Is Not Wrong
paragraphs: Next, sort your concerns into two groups.
Some are ==preferences==: you would have picked another framework or named things differently.
Others are risks: the plan will miss the deadline, or it will lose data under load.
Only the second group should block the proposal.
Label the first group clearly, with something like "personal preference, feel free to ignore."
**Reviewers who block on taste soon find that nobody asks them to review anything.**
For real risks, be concrete and ==proportionate==.
Explain the ==impact==, how likely it is, and what would reduce it.
A rare edge case does not deserve the same energy as a likely outage.
If the author ==addresses== the risk in a way you would not have chosen, __let it go__.
Your job is to make the proposal safe, not to turn it into yours.
Authors remember the reviewers who __made their ideas stronger__, and they come back to them.
paragraphs_zh: 接下来，把你的顾虑分成两类。
一类是个人偏好：你可能会选另一个框架，或者换种命名方式。
另一类是风险：这个方案会赶不上 deadline，或者高负载下会丢数据。
只有第二类才应该卡住这份提案。
第一类要明确标出来，比如写一句「个人偏好，可以忽略」。
因为个人口味就卡别人的评审人，很快会发现没人再找他们 review 了。
对真正的风险，要说得具体，也要把握分寸。
讲清楚影响有多大、发生的可能性有多高，以及怎么能降低它。
一个很少触发的边界情况，不值得花跟一个大概率故障同样的力气。
如果作者用一种你不会选的方式解决了这个风险，那就随它去吧。
你的任务是让提案变得安全，不是把它改成你的方案。
作者会记住那些让他们的想法变得更强的评审人，下次还会去找他们。

gist.q: 评审一个你不认同的方案，第一步应该做什么？
gist.a: 先替方案说话：写下作者的目标和最有力的论点，并问作者「我理解得对吗」。
及早发现误解（很多分歧其实是对同一页的不同理解）；让作者感到被认真对待，更愿意听后面的意见。

gist.q: 作者建议把顾虑分成哪两类？分别怎么处理？
gist.a: 个人偏好（标注清楚、可忽略，不阻塞）和真实风险（具体、成比例地说明影响、可能性和缓解办法，才可以阻塞）。

prompts.q: 另一个团队提议把服务从 Go 迁到 Java，你不认同。评审会上先用 30 秒复述对方方案的目标和最强论点，再确认理解是否正确。
prompts.ref: Before I share my concerns, let me check that I understand the proposal. The main goal is to put all backend services on one language, so engineers can move between teams and share libraries. The strongest argument, I think, is the hiring data: most of our new hires already know Java. Did I get that right? If so, my questions are really about the migration cost, not the direction.
prompts.ref_zh: 在说我的顾虑之前，我先确认一下我对提案的理解。主要目标是把所有后端服务统一成一种语言，这样工程师可以在团队之间流动，也能共享库。我觉得最有力的论据是招聘数据：我们大部分新人本来就会 Java。我理解得对吗？如果对的话，我的问题其实是关于迁移成本的，而不是方向。

prompts.q: 你对一个方案有三条意见，其中两条只是个人偏好，一条是真实风险。用 30 秒把它们区分清楚地讲出来。
prompts.ref: I have three comments, but only one of them is blocking. The first two are just preferences: I'd name the topics differently, and I'd use a different retry library. Feel free to ignore both. The real concern is data loss. If the consumer crashes after reading a message but before writing to the database, that message is gone. I'd like to see that case handled before we approve.
prompts.ref_zh: 我有三条评论，但只有一条是 blocking。前两条只是个人偏好：topic 我会换个命名，重试库我会用另一个。这两条都可以忽略。真正的顾虑是丢数据。如果 consumer 读到消息后、写数据库之前挂了，这条消息就没了。我希望在批准之前，把这种情况处理掉。

words.ex: Her insight about cold starts changed the whole design.
I have a bias toward tools I've used before, so push back if needed.
Half the debate was a misunderstanding about what "real time" meant.
The team was more receptive once we showed the cost numbers.
Tabs versus spaces is a preference, not a blocker.
Keep the fix proportionate to the risk; this is an internal tool.
What's the user impact if this job runs an hour late?
The new version addresses the timeout issue I raised.
Can you give a concrete example of where this would fail?
